subject: Post-signature MAP & activation sprint (Pulseway Analytics)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@pulseway.com>, Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@pulseway.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Post-signature MAP & activation sprint (Pulseway Analytics)

Congrats again on signing, Hannah & Marco — excited to get you live. Attached is a first-draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds the implementation cadence: rollout windows, canary plan, migration checkpoints, and training calendar. I pulled the timelines we discussed on the call into explicit owners and acceptance gates to avoid ambiguity.

High-level ask: please review the attached MAP_v1 and confirm the following by EOD Wednesday so we can lock the first two sprint targets:
- Canary window preference (weekday 10/11–10/15 or weekend 10/17–10/18)
- Primary SSO test account and an ops contact for canary-day escalation
- Any org-level blackout dates for October/November rollout

What I included in the sheet: kickoff & sprint schedule, migration cutover steps (DB export → staged ingest → traffic shift), training plan (train-the-trainer + end-user webinars), success metrics for canary (error rate, 95th p95 latency, failover time), rollback criteria, and a security attestation summary we will provide to your compliance team.

Attachments: Pulseway_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + milestone tracker), security-attestation-summary.pdf

Next internal step: Marissa and Soojin, can you take ownership of the canary runbook and the training materials respectively? I’ll follow up with a short internal checklist.

Thanks —
Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@pulseway.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@pulseway.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-signature MAP & activation sprint (Pulseway Analytics)

Ben — thanks for the draft. Quick notes after a skim:
1) Weekend canary is preferable for our ops team — less user traffic. Weekend of 10/17–10/18 works.
2) Ops contact: Marco Diaz (cc'd) will be the escalation lead. Marco's primary cell is +1-415-210-4562.
3) Blackout: we have a major marketing push on 11/02, so please avoid any risky migrations that week.

I'll review the MAP in detail and aim to come back with annotated comments by Tuesday. The security attestation looks fine at a glance; I'll loop in our InfoSec if they want more.

Hannah
VP Product, Pulseway Analytics

Team — copying the internal note I promised. Pulseway prefers weekend canary 10/17–10/18 and Marco is the ops lead. Key owners below:
- Marissa: canary runbook + cutover command sequence (DB snapshot steps, staged ingest, traffic switch) — due 10/06 for review
- Soojin: training syllabus, trainer materials, and two live train-the-trainer sessions (10/05, 10/12) — deliverables: slide deck + recorded walkthrough
- Vanessa: post-cutover monitoring dashboard (SLO widgets: p95 latency, token error rate, throughput) + alert thresholds — due 10/09

Pre-flight checklist (actionable):
- Obtain Marco's production test account and service role by 10/01 (Ben)
- Run a smoke importer against the staging bucket and validate schema parity (Marissa)
- Share the security attestation with Pulseway InfoSec and collect any additional ask (Ben)

I set tentative internal review sessions on 10/07 and 10/14 (30 min each) to walk the runbook and training content. Please flag conflicts.

Ben

A couple of requests from our engineers:
- Can you add a short checklist item in the MAP for token rotation immediately post-cutover? We want a documented window to rotate and validate keys (avoid lingering tokens).
- We'll need 90 minutes of overlap with Redwood ops during the traffic switch on 10/17; suggest 10:00–11:30 PT.

I attached nothing here — the MAP file looks good so far.
